apps.author: Muntashir Akon

release.changelog:
App Manager v4.1.1 improves permissions, installation, ADB connectivity, and several other parts of the application. Visit Settings > About > Version/Changelog for details.

**Revoke Internet Permission**
App Manager can now block internet for individual applications utilizing the eBPF rules in root or ADB mode. To block internet for an application, go to the "Uses permissions" tab and click on the toggle button next to `android.permission.INTERNET` to revoke the permission.
  
_Known Limitation._ The eBPF rules are lost after a reboot. App Manager attempts to restore the rules right after a reboot. However, in ADB mode, it might take a while to connect to wireless debugging depending on the availability of a Wi-Fi connection. This might allow applications that start after a reboot to use internet.  

**Others**
- Added support for editing `.bat` files  
- Improved installation reliability and performance  
- Improved permission management  
- Improved ADB pairing, connections, and mode handling  
- Improved settings transitions and startup messages  
- Fixed displaying profiles after creating a profile for the first time  
- Fixed intercepting browser URLs  
- Fixed listing applications on Android 17  
- Fixed title ordering in What's New dialog.  

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/AppManager/compare/v4.1.0...v4.1.1

release.changelog:
> [!NOTE]
> ## Release Highlights
> This release fixes the recent video playback issues and that playlists contain no videos.
> 
> To overcome the video playback issues, we implemented YouTube's new, custom streaming protocol (called SABR). YouTube started to progressively remove support for traditional streaming protocols, so LibreTube's support for the new protocol should make video playback much more reliable.
> 
> Apart from this, the release includes support for podcasts and courses tabs on channels, a "resume all" option for downloads, as well as many minor bug fixes and small improvements.

- [`a2b30e1`](https://github.com/libre-tube/LibreTube/commit/a2b30e17a696e0326c5686c6df3c3804beba6c9a) - database migration crashes app on Android 13 and below *(commit by @Bnyro)*

The `api29` APK has been removed and replaced with `allstorage`, which uses the "manage external storage" permission to allow unrestricted file access without having to downgrade the API level.
It will stay separate and not be shipped to Google Play.

### :arrow_down_small: Which APK do I download? :arrow_down_small: 

You generally want to get **`arm64-v8a`**. Try `armeabi-v7a` for old devices. Or `x86` otherwise.
If you are unsure then the `universal` APK will work everywhere.

release.changelog:
### New Features

- Greatly optimized TV controls
- Added support for video quality selection in live streams
- The "Swipe down to minimize" gesture is now configurable in Settings
- Optimized the deletion interaction for content filters
- Added support for Recommended/Popular live streams (NicoNico)
- Added support for the Live tab on channels (NicoNico)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed the "Start in fullscreen" setting not working
- Fixed split-screen mode being unavailable
- Fixed an issue where subtitles would disappear when entering fullscreen mode
- Fixed content blocking not applying to public playlists
- Fixed an issue where live streams continued to fetch data while paused
- Fixed an issue where terminated videos using the SABR protocol could not be resumed
- Fixed a crash that could occur when starting playback under specific conditions
- Fixed an issue where the total playlist duration would increase infinitely in certain scenarios
- Fixed a crash caused by deleting watch history under specific conditions
- Fixed the dislike counter not being disabled by default on fresh installations
- Fixed download failures occurring under specific conditions (BiliBili)
- Fixed recommended live streams appearing empty (BiliBili)

<hr/>
If you're enjoying PipePipe, please help share it with your friends. Every bit of support means a lot to us!
<hr/>

### Which APK should you download?

- arm64-v8a should work on most devices.
- armeabi-v7a if your device is a 15+ year old phone.
- x86_64 for 64-bit Android simulators (on a PC).
- x86 for 32-bit simulators.
